newsitem.title: UK: Insurance changes put pressure on ratings - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Insurance changes put pressure on ratings - S&P.

text.p: Fundamental changes in the insurance industry could lead to downgrades in credit ratings, Standard & Poor's managing director of insurance ratings told a news conference on Monday.

Reduced underwriting, slow growth in demand, the drive for decreased distribution expenses and the increasing mobility of capital are some of the problems affecting the industry. "Against a background of economic stability, the insurance sector is undergoing fundmental changes," said Andrew Campbell-Hart, S&P's managing director of insurance ratings. "Technical and structural changes are exerting downward pressure on ratings."

He said 1996 had seen consoldations in the sector, with a trend towards "mega mergers and mega acquisitions". He noted that more insurance companies were upgraded than downgraded in 1996, but said this was at odds with the overall pressures.
"The only bright note in the sector is the increasing realisation that private pension provision in Europe must increase," said Campbell-Hart.
Asked about whether S&P intended to provide a rating for Lloyd's of London, he said he was not aware that the agency had ever rated an entire market place.
